chunks: Say: "If Ar-Rahman had a son I would have been the first of worshippers."

key_terms.الرَّحْمٰنِ: Ar-Rahman (The Merciful, often used for a specific deity or attribute of God)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says 'If Ar-Rahman had a son, I would be the first to worship him'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a rhetorical challenge by God to the polytheists of Mecca, asserting that if their deity Al-Rahman possessed offspring, the Prophet Muhammad would be the first to worship him, thereby exposing the logical inconsistency of their belief. It underscores the concept of *Tawhid* (divine unity) by contrasting the created nature of false gods with the absolute sovereignty of Allah, a theme central to Shia theological discourse on prophetic authority and divine oneness.
